beats.intent: The core problem is that compact thought state does not directly match the dense spatial field super-resolution needs.
beats.claim: CTM's thought representation is compact; super-resolution needs a dense spatial field.
beats.narration: The method begins with a representation mismatch: a compact thinking process has to produce spatial detail at every output location.

params.headline: Compact thought must produce dense image detail
params.sub: ThinkSR adapts CTM for lightweight super-resolution.

beats.intent: The method is positioned between a plain CTM, a window-wise adaptation, and DQ-CTM.
beats.claim: CTM, a window-wise adaptation, and DQ-CTM compared.
beats.narration: The comparison separates the original compact formulation from a window-wise variant and the DQ-CTM design used for dense reconstruction. The CTM reference establishes the compact thought side of the mismatch. The window-wise adaptation connects that process to local image regions. DQ-CTM is the version presented as the super-resolution path.

params.headline: DQ-CTM is framed against two CTM variants

beats.intent: The low-resolution image is encoded into a dense feature carrier, then partitioned into windows.
beats.narration: The carrier starts as features encoded from the low-resolution input. The dense feature field is the persistent state that can be read and updated. Windowing turns that field into the units processed by the compact thought mechanism. The equation names the path from image to carrier to windows.

params.headline: The dense carrier is built before thought updates it

beats.intent: ThinkSR runs encoder, windowing, shared DQ-CTM ticks, and decoder as one end-to-end path.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The end-to-end path keeps the dense carrier present while compact thought operates over windows. The encoder creates the feature field from the input image. The window stage exposes local spatial chunks to the thought process. Shared DQ-CTM ticks apply the same compact update process repeatedly. The decoder turns the updated carrier back into the super-resolved image.

params.headline: ThinkSR updates a dense carrier through shared ticks
params.note: The method keeps a persistent dense carrier.

beats.intent: Reconstruction is shown evolving from T=0 through T=4 against bicubic and ground truth.
beats.claim: Reconstruction at T=0 through T=4 against bicubic and ground truth.
beats.narration: The ticks are presented as a visible reconstruction sequence rather than only as an internal computation. The first reconstruction anchors the starting point of the iterative process. Later ticks show the same output after repeated DQ-CTM updates. Bicubic and ground truth provide the visual references for the sequence.

params.headline: The reconstruction is tracked across DQ-CTM ticks

beats.intent: Absolute-error maps compare the same crops on one shared colour scale.
beats.claim: Absolute-error maps on the same crops, one shared colour scale.
beats.narration: The error view changes the comparison from image appearance to per-crop residuals. The same crops keep the visual comparison controlled. A shared colour scale makes the error maps directly comparable. The figure therefore tests reconstruction quality without changing the crop or scale.

params.headline: Error maps use the same crops and colour scale

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is competitive with the listed CNN baselines on average benchmark score.
beats.claim: Competitive with CNN baselines; behind recent lightweight transformers.
beats.narration: The average scores put DQ-CTM-SR in the same narrow band as the CNN baselines. CARN reports an average of 28.970. IMDN reports 28.968. RFDN reports 29.022. DQ-CTM-SR reports 28.983, which is close to those CNN results.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is close to the CNN baselines
params.note: Average is reported for x4 lightweight super-resolution.

beats.intent: The reported average leaves DQ-CTM-SR behind the recent lightweight transformer baseline CATANet.
beats.claim: Competitive with CNN baselines; behind recent lightweight transformers.
beats.narration: The same benchmark table also shows the main reported gap. DQ-CTM-SR reports an average of 28.983. CATANet reports 29.482. That makes CATANet the stronger result among the listed methods.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR trails CATANet on average score
params.note: CATANet is the recent lightweight transformer baseline in the table.

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model among the reported lightweight methods.
beats.claim: Table 1 — x4 lightweight super-resolution, average over five benchmarks.
beats.narration: The parameter counts show that compact thought does not make this version the smallest model in the table. CATANet reports 0.535 million parameters. RFDN reports 0.550 million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR reports 1.129 million parameters. CARN remains the largest listed model at 1.592 million parameters.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is mid-sized among the listed models

beats.intent: ThinkSR's contribution is the persistent dense carrier updated by compact thought, with results close to CNNs but below CATANet.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The source's central idea is not that compact thought replaces spatial structure. It is that a dense carrier stays present while compact thought reads and updates it. The reported outcome is competitive with CNN baselines. The stated limitation is that recent lightweight transformers remain ahead.

params.headline: ThinkSR keeps density outside the compact thought state
